utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll wait for the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radovanovic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take up at 1D5335 in e-court. While we wait for that, I can introduce it as the original Milosevic case report prepared by Dr. Tabeau which she updated for purposes of preparing P2798 on the same topic in the Mladic case. And once we get that document, I'd be looking for page 8 in Serbian, page 7 in English. And it should be ... it should be the third paragraph visible from the top in the Serbian and in English -- now we're getting ... Is this the... yes. Okay. And it's the last two lines in the English that we look at, or actually the second-to-last line, where Dr. Tabeau says: "Note that our definitions of internally displaced persons and refugees are statistical, not legal." Professor, are you able to assist us in understanding Dr. Tabeau by telling us what, if any, definition exists in statistics for internally displaced persons and refugees?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In statistics, there is no definition of refugees and internally displaced persons. This is a definition made up by the Prosecution expert who does not define it. She doesn't say, By the statistical definition, I mean this and that. Concerning refugees and internally displaced persons, we usually use the UN definition. If an author, writing a paper, wants to provide his own definition, then he cannot call it statistical definition because there is no statistical definition. There is no universal statistical definition but the author, of course, has the right to use the definition that he wants. However, he has to explain it so that we can see whether it coincides with what is normally used in science.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to the report of Dr. Tabeau for the Mladic case, which is P2798. And while we wait for that, Professor, do you have any observations or conclusions as to the manner in which Dr. Tabeau has analysed migrations of what she has referred to as refugees and internally displaced persons in this report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a way that is exclusively applied according to the methodology that they created. It has nothing to do with scientific methodology. It is the way in which they adapted to themselves the research in order to get the results they needed. Dr. Tabeau, among other things, holds the position that what they were doing, although I objected to it and possibly other experts, she holds the position that nothing needs to be changed. They cited reasons like it took them so long to correct the material, et cetera. That is no valid justification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, you said yesterday that Dr. Tabeau used administrative divisions, territorial divisions, created after the war and this was at transcript page 38166 onwards. What is the effect of Dr. Tabeau basing her results on administrative divisions in territory created after the war?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that way, you show results that appear much more dramatic than if you showed them at the level of the administrative and territorial division from 1991. The fact is that Bosnia and Herzegovina was divided administratively and territorially in a different way, and Dr. Tabeau was entitled to apply that new division, but only if she explained why she deviates from the division, the territorial division, at the time of the indictment. If there is a reason, and if that reason is important and valid in the opinion of Dr. Tabeau, then she could have said, We will be doing everything in accordance with the new administrative division because that provides for a better representation, it's easier to get the results, et cetera. It was certainly not easier in terms of time because all the censuses were done according to the old administrative division. So you had to adjust even censuses to the new administrative division, grouping settlements and territories in line with the new division. I don't know what Dr. Tabeau thought. Maybe she thought that she -- if she applied the new administrative division, some results would be more clearly represented and the changes would appear much more important. If you view these changes at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina without that administrative and territorial division, they don't have that crucial importance. There is no crucial difference in these migrations that were completely wrongly calculated, by the way. What's interesting in her application of that administrative division is that I don't know how important it is if you compare it to the territory that Dr. Tabeau calls the Mladic territory, and she defines it as holding 26 municipalities. She never made a distinction by saying, for instance, the Mladic territory compared to the total territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina shows this and that. Or the Mladic territory relative to the BH Federation shows such and such changes. She just presents certain results without explaining. I'm not denying her right to apply the new administrative division but it would be intellectually honest to explain why she believes that this administrative division is better than applying the old one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 27 in English and it will be page 30 in the Serbian, I believe we'll arrive at Table 1 of this report, P2798?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could I ask one additional question. You said in that way you show results that appear much more dramatic than if you showed them at the level of the administrative territorial division from 1991. Could you explain or have you calculated the outcome which is dramatically more? Could you tell us, is it 1 per cent, 10 per cent? What's the outcome if do you it in the way you suggest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I were looking at a particular table, it would help me to explain what I meant. If you say that the changes to the ethnic structure at the level of Bosnia appears such and such, for instance, there were 40 per cent Bosniaks and 45 per cent Serbs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a second. You said it would give a dramatically different outcome. Could you tell us what your outcome is which dramatically differs from Dr. Tabeau's outcome and where could you illustrate that? Not in general terms, not in the abstract but just to say this is what she did, that's her outcome, this is how it should have been done. And you see the outcome is dramatically different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have to have a table in front of me. I'm trying to explain what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The table of Dr. Tabeau. I don't mind, any table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, choose whatever or let Mr. Ivetic choose whatever which gives such a dramatic different outcome. I mean, you're stating it in general terms [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... so that I can show where the difference lies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I leave it entirely up to you and to Mr. Ivetic to show it. In the terms as I asked you to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can tell that you in the report of the professor at page 57 of the English, there's Figure number 4 which we be will getting to later in the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say we'll come to that, then I'll wait. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can -- there we go. Now we have both languages on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, here we have the table of Dr. Tabeau talking about citizens, total number of citizens by nationality. And, first of all, looking at the percentages shown by Dr. Tabeau, are these percentages true demographic indicators?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see very well but in the first one, where it says population in 1991, Dr. Tabeau shows -- I think this is 40.1 per cent Serbs. There were -- I can't see very well - 40.9 per cent Muslims. Now I see perfectly well. So the first three columns where it says: Population in 1991 and then it says: All nationalities million and something. Serbs 416.000, and that makes up 41.1 per cent of the total population. Muslims 414.000, and that makes 40.9 per cent of the total population. And it goes on by ethnicity. These are the shares of individual ethnicities in the total population for the Mladic territory that Dr. Tabeau calculated or assessed in a very bad way. I will accept it as it is, and I did not go into elaborate explanations. But this assessment, this estimate, where she explains that the census on the Mladic territory, the population, was assessed by her, by taking all the population aged 18 and up, and saying that this population is comparable to the voters. That is the population that she found in the voting lists and in 1995, she established them as the population in the Mladic territory. What's missing here? In this census, there is a million or so population for these two -- 22 municipalities. That was the situation in 1991. These results, this outcome of the census -- this outcome of the census is certainly correct. However, one must bear in mind that the population derived from Dr. Tabeau from the voting lists reflects voters who voluntarily registered in 1997. So in this category, age 18 and up, there is a number of dead persons who died between 1991 and 1997. Let me stop at that and not mention anything else. Dr. Tabeau, if she wanted to make a proper comparison, because among the voters she has only living people, she should have tried to cleanse the census from 1991 and subtract all those who died between 1991 and 1997, at least from natural causes. I know this is not an easy job, but I know also that Dr. Tabeau has the document commissioned by the Tribunal reflecting the statistics of Republika Srpska and the statistics of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it also shows the mortality calculated by all standard rules. Dr. Brunborg even estimates that this document that in statistics is called DEM3 is excellent. In particular, for Republika Srpska. So she has a source containing over 160.000 people recorded as dead between 1991 and 1995. Out of those 160.000 people, about 66.000 died of natural causes. So only for the period 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1996, and 1997 -- sorry. Between 1992 and 1995 inclusive, around 60.000 people died of natural causes, the rest are violent deaths. In a way -- not in a way. These numbers are inflated. I know it's a very big job. But if thousands of names and surnames were corrected over the years, it would have been only fair, since she has the information, it would have been fair for the doctor to include a footnote saying, The estimate of this population number is not correct because it includes all the dead -- deaths from April 1991 to 1997 inclusive. But we don't know even how many people died in 1996, 1997 and 1998, although we have statistical data. The figure would then be much higher than 140.000. The next thing you would have to show me the population for 1997. You just have to move the table a little. Here it is. In this column, where it says: Sample of population from 1997 -- maybe it's a matter of translation; I don't know. An expert cannot give a sample of the population. He can say estimate, but this is not an estimate. He can say population obtained by matching. But never mind. Let's accept it as it is. Earlier on she called it estimate. This sample of the population from 1997 represents the result obtained by matching the electoral list with the census. In her reports, experts claim that they had matched electoral lists with the census and got 80 per cent of all the people. I think this is overreaching because Dr. Brunborg shows that out of 2.7 million voters, according to some matching keys that are relatively acceptable, a million and a half people were matched. A million and a half out of 2.7 million is not 70 per cent -- 80 per cent. It means that the rest were matched according to some criteria that only they know. Dr. Brunborg doesn't show them or shows them only partially. So, if what she obtained by matching - Dr. Tabeau - then she should have said out of which number. If, in the Mladic territory, there are, for instance, 500.000 population, she could have matched 256.000. We don't know. Only Dr. Tabeau knows how many total population there were. Only Dr. Tabeau knows which percentage of the total this number is. We have to take it at their word and believe that 80 per cent were matched in -- in all ethnic communities. That's what I believe is intellectually dishonest. You should say, I have registered voters in the Mladic territory, so many. I matched so many. All these errors, I would be able to tolerate even if they were not honestly shown. However, what is absolutely inadmissible in statistics is the manipulation of this parameter. You will see plus 25.3 per cent. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if we could move the table a little bit to the right in both versions so that both percentages can be seen. I think it will assist us in what the professor is talking about. Professor, we have now -- that's fine. If we can do the same in English. We have now for the first entry, 41.1 per cent, and then we have 51.4 per cent, and we have reflected that it is an increase of plus 25.3 per cent. Could you please continue your answer, taking into account now these percentages that we see in front of us.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In all of her conclusions, Dr. Tabeau, in her report states, the number of Serbs in the Mladic territory has increased by 25.3 per cent, the number of Muslims decreased by 8 per cent. Everything you see in the last column of this table, these relative figures, this is a sort of manipulation because Dr. Tabeau failed to show the difference between the participation of Serbs in 1991 of whom there were 41.1 per cent and the participation of Serbs she arrived at according to the voters' list which is 51.4 per cent. The difference between these two figures is not 25.3 per cent. It is 10 per cent. But what did she do? She introduced a non-demographic parameter as a demographic one and said, Well, if you understand it, fine; if you don't, that's fine as well. She said the following. The changes of percentages -- I apologise. I keep making the same mistake. She said the change of percentages in this ethnic group between 1991 and 1997. What does that mean? It means that the percentage of 51 per cent was 25.3 per cent bigger than the percentage of 41.1. Pardon me, she didn't need to show the changes of percentages but the changes of shares in the overall ethnic structure. What she is showing is not the way that would make clear to everyone as to what had happened. She has her Ph.D. in the demography of mathematics and, of course, it can be useful in some of her papers or some forecasts and so forth, but to present such information to the Tribunal is something I believe to be very unprofessional, and I consider it manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. You said it's not 25.3 per cent; it's 10 per cent. She says that she presents the change in the percentage. Now, the percentage went up by 25 percent, and the overall percentage was 10 per cent higher. 10 per cent on 40 per cent is 25 percent. I mean, it's just a way of -- it's not -- you say it's wrong. I mean, it's just what you wished to present. If you say, Well, I would have wished she presented something else. But to say it should be 10 per cent and not 25 percent entirely depends on what you are presenting. Isn't it? I mean, there can hardly be any dispute that 51.4 is 25 percent more than 41.1. And she explains what she presents and by saying what she does is wrong, you mainly emphasise that you would have wished that she had presented something else. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm saying this: In demographic studies, things are not presented that way, especially not so if it involves such demographic studies that should be clear to everyone. To discuss the change of percentage in her conclusion, she asserts that the participation of the Serbian population, the share of the Serbian population in the Mladic territory, changed by 25.3 per cent upwards. She didn't say that the percentage of the share increased. If Dr. Tabeau wanted to present it this way, she could not have arrived at that particular conclusion. In her conclusions, as you can see, she states that the share of Serbs is increased by 25.3, the participation of the share of Muslims is so much less and so on and so forth. She doesn't say that the percentage of Serbs in the overall shares changed for this and that much. So she doesn't explain it fairly or honestly. As I said, I'm not saying she cannot rely on this and perhaps in some studies one may well do so, but I have not had occasion to see such a study. But when you are interpreting it, when are you drawing a conclusion you cannot say that the share changed by 25 percent. You say the percentage of the share changed by 25 percent and then it's clear to everyone. Please look at the conclusions drawn by Mrs. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't that exactly what she says at the top of the column where she says: 1991 to 1997 change (percentage) in percentages? So she is telling us that the percentage -- percentual change is the percentages is 25 per cent. And I still -- I mean, you may consider that it's wiser to present something else but here it is a percentual change percentages and that seems to me to be the right number because 41.1 plus 25 percent makes 51 per cent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, then she should state so in her conclusion. And in her conclusion, she does not. You, or anyone else for that matter, when reading the report will definitely not go back to check if she is mentioning the change of percentages. The conclusion should therefore be as such. The percentage of the share of Serbs in the share in 1991 compared to the share in 1997 changed by 25 percent, but that is not the formulation of her conclusion and in the overall context we do not get that picture. She doesn't discuss the change of percentage but the change of share.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I am afraid that I have to disappoint you that when reading the report that we definitely would not go back to check what she was mentioning, because that's what we do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I just put one additional question for a clarification. Several times now used the term "Mladic territory," and you introduced that term in page -- on page 4, line 19. You said: The territory that Dr. Tabeau calls the Mladic territory. Can we please move both tables to the left. Further, further, further. If you look here, it's slightly different: Mladic case area, instead of Mladic territory. Would you agree that "Mladic territory" is not used, at least not in this table by Ms. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my parlance when I say "the territory or area," it amounts to the same. I didn't mean to say that it was his area. It is the area covered by the Mladic case, i.e., the territory referred to in the Mladic case. It's a synonym. Perhaps I didn't choose the words too carefully but, to me, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Mladic case area is perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. But you introduced it as if Dr. Tabeau used the term "Mladic territory," and "Mladic territory" and "Mladic case area" is slightly different and I think it's -- if you want to present your opinion perfectly correct then you should use your language perfectly correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. When I say "the Mladic territory," it's synonymous with the term "area." I apologize. Dr. Tabeau's definition is perfectly fine; Mladic case area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you omitted the word "case." This is the problem. Mr. Ivetic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page and Dr. Tabeau's Table 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Professor, I would again ask you in relation to this table if you would have any additional comments or things that you had wished to point out.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need the table to be enlarged, please. I can't see. Perhaps a little bit more so I can see. I can only see 1997. Perhaps now I could explain what I wanted to say when Judge Orie asked me what would be the difference if she divided between Republika Srpska and the Federation of BiH. I can't see the table very well. Could I have it all on the screen? If you look at the total figures for the Mladic case area, you will see the changes in total, irrespective of the old or new administrative division. When you look at this Mladic case area, you see that Dr. Tabeau divided it between the RS and the FBiH and then can you see much more drastic changes per ethnicity then they actually amount to in the overall figure. This is what I meant when I said that Dr. Tabeau applied the new administrative division because then the figures appear much more bombastic, as I said. According to the new division, the figures appear such but according to the old division the figures appear as they are here. Now whether this is the true situation according to the new administrative division is something we don't know, because the way these figures were arrived at, by matching, occurred without the figure of how many millions or hundreds of thousands of people were excluded because they were not matched so as to account for these differences. This is what I believed to be, in a way, Dr. Tabeau's wish to accentuate certain things without providing a proper administration on why she relied on the new administrative division rather than the old one. If she wanted to stress that, she should have introduced a footnote to explain. She had to go through all of her sources by applying the new administrative division because the census was conducted according to the old one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you say it's bombastic and at the same time you say we do not know exactly because Dr. Tabeau has not explained it. If it has not been explained, how could you draw the conclusion that it's bombastic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the table back, please, the whole of it. Not this one. The one per ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be the prior page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have that in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if we look in e-court then, of course, we could have, as it is now, it is now presented in e-court on the English public view, then you see that now we have the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why do I believe it to be the case? If you look at the Mladic case area, for example, in 1997 what was the share of Serbs in the overall number of Serbs located by Dr. Tabeau, and you see that the figure is 51.4 per cent. When she relies on the Mladic case area, in order to divide it between Republika Srpska and the Federation of BiH, the figure you arrive at is 90 per cent as opposed to 4.5, and then she mentions which municipalities are in the Federation and which are in the Republika Srpska. I have this position: If some of the municipalities were not divided before 1991 and now, all of a sudden, they are, if we don't know if some settlements were left out, then if we have the example of a divided municipality, it doesn't mean anything to say that the population went this way or that. They were simply divided. Some of them remained, while others were entered administratively into a new unit. So that is why I say that there should have been an explanation why Dr. Tabeau believed that relying on the new administrative division was better than using the administrative division that was in place at the time of events of which Mr. Mladic stands accused. If these charges refer to certain years when the -- the old division was in place, why use the new one? I'm not making a big deal of this. I'm just asking why. My conclusion need not necessarily be correct, but it is not correct because there was no honest explanation as to why she used the new division. She doesn't explain whether in these divided settlements she managed to account `for all of the population or whether some of it was dropped out. How many municipalities out of the total number of municipalities in the Mladic case area are now in the RS although one can calculate that on the basis of this table. In any case, I believe that would have been an honest explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you considered the possibility that Dr. Tabeau used the Mladic case area as the basis for her findings in order to get rid of any administrative changes but, rather, focuses on geographic changes, that is, village by village, town by town, so as to not distort the picture through these administrative changes? Have you considered that she may have done so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Tabeau said plainly that she would provide data according to the new administrative division, and she had explained that in her previous reports such as the one in the Milosevic case. So there was nothing for me to ponder. In the Samac report and Odzak report she also used the new division. In the Slobodan Milosevic report she used the new division. In that report, she even states that we left out a certain number of settlements because of the division of municipalities but there were very few. I won't even go into what kind of figure that is. So from the start Dr. Tabeau relied on this idea of the new division. I am not against that, but I want an explanation. It would have been intellectually honest for her to explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that she excluded only a small number of settlements or -- have you verified whether that reflects the change in the administrative structure? I mean, apparently - and that's how I understand your answer - that she has considered, to some extent, I don't know to what extent, and I'm inviting you to tell us whether it was complete or not, that she has considered that the administrative changes may have led to shifting one settlement to another administrative entity, and, therefore, has apparently corrected for the administrative changes. Do you know how complete that correction has been? Have you verified that, whether it was -- because you're criticizing it, which is fine. But have you then identified in what respect she has not adjusted and to what extent she has corrected the administrative changes by focussing on geographical - that is, by settlement, or by town - the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's not what I say. Dr. Tabeau, in the Milosevic report, stated that there were some minor problems - I'm paraphrasing - of course, I can try and locate it and quote it precisely. There were minor problems because the new administrative division divided some settlements, not only municipalities, but that a small number of settlements and small amounts of population were left out. I don't know what that figure is. I didn't check that. It didn't occur to me to do that. I trust Dr. Tabeau, that it was the case, that there were problems because there were divisions of settlements. But when she said "small changes," I was wondering what the figure is? Tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands? Millions? That's not what I say. That's what Dr. Tabeau stated. And if I may add one more thing. Administrative territory division is a political matter. It has got nothing to do with any geographic divisions. Dr. Tabeau did not take into account any geographical divisions. She relied on the existing new administrative territorial division, and she is certainly aware of the old division because the entire 1991 census was done according to the old administrative division. The difference between the new and old administrative territorial division is the Dayton line which divided Bosnia-Herzegovina into two entities. It occurred as it did, dividing certain municipalities, and when you do that, it means dividing certain settlements as well. This is what I was talking about. I didn't try to control whether the administrative division according to the Dayton Accords was correct and whether Dr. Tabeau applied the correct principles. She didn't come up with that. She simply took it from the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina which exists now because the statistics done now, is done according to the new administrative division after the war. I was just wondering why she was making things more complicated for herself. In a way, she had to translate a number of sources done according to the old division into this new division, and it was key, key to prove that these people actually existed and that they were alive in 1991. It was very important for them to use it in order to extrapolate the number of refugees and IDPs. It was also crucial to have it so that from the census itself, they could take the figures pertaining to the ethnic makeup. So how was it that it was simpler to rely on the new division instead of reconciling the figures between old and new. The more simple thing would be to rely on the old division because their key source, the census, was based on it. When matching, she did not offer any further explanations in terms of how it was done. They used a total number of people instead of the territorial division. If she wanted to calculate the ethnic makeup, the ethnic structure, one needs to bear in mind that no voter is assigned to an ethnic group in the voter list. It simply doesn't exist in the voting lists. For Dr. Tabeau to pin-point who is a Serb, Muslim or anyone of any other ethnicity, she simply matched the voters' lists with the census and if she came across a Svetlana Radovanovic who declared herself to be a Serb, if she has a voter by that name, she concludes that the voter is Serb. The census was the basis for any kind of matching. That was my reasoning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then one short question. You say she corrected the new administrative -- the administrative changes, she corrected for that. And she said these were minor corrections. And you say, if I understand you, well, I don't know whether these were minor or that there should have been major corrections, I am unable to verify what she did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not saying that Dr. Tabeau made corrections. Dr. Tabeau can get a new administrative territorial division. Bosnia-Herzegovina is carrying out a new administrative territorial division. That is done at state level. It is political, so she received information about the new administrative territorial division in which she sees that there are many divided municipalities and divided settlements. If Dr. Tabeau wants to deal with the population, she talks to the statistics people in Sarajevo and she says, I have a divided settlement. Never mind what the name is. According to Dayton, now it's called Novo Ljubovija, New Ljubovija, and there's another one Stara Ljubovija, Old Ljubovija. How can I know what the new number of inhabitants is and what is the old number? The statistics office has information on the basis of which they can get data about the part that is now a new settlement or a new municipality and what the situation was in 1991. It wasn't done by Dr. Tabeau. Perhaps she addressed them to ask for this but this is something that Dr. Tabeau cannot do without these offices but you have to understand that these lines are not ideal. Dr. Tabeau is just saying that in the new administrative territorial division a certain number of settlements has been left out -- no, sorry, number of inhabitants and that's a small number. If the doctor knows -- it's not that she did the calculations herself, it's probably the statistics people. And then you say yes, two per cent of the inhabitants have been left out for the municipality, say, Odzak because the settlement was divided and we could not, in the census, determine whether they wept left or right. So it's not Dr. Tabeau that she -- that made the new divisions. She applied the decisions that had been made. Now I'm just asking the following. If she applied this why doesn't she put it in a footnote and why doesn't she say, yes, this is a better division than the old one. Simple because she has sources, sources that are the old administrative divisions. That's a key source and I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness earlier expressed an interest in perhaps referring to the text that Dr. Tabeau had, and if it's of assistance I believe that what she's referring to is P2788, English e-court page 6 and B/C/S page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Ivetic. I think it's time for a break. It's sometimes a bit lost when reference is made to reports when we do not know exactly if these reports are in evidence before us, yes or no, and to the extent you're able to assist us, that would be appreciated. We take a break, and, Ms. Radovanovic, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, I'd like to put a few scheduling matters on the record. The first: Having indicated to the parties on the 9th of July, that the Chamber was considering a change in the sitting schedule for the week beginning the 14th of September, the following is now placed on the record: The Chamber will not sit on Monday, the 14th of September, and will start hearings at the normal time on Tuesday, the 15th of September. The Chamber will also sit on Friday, the 18th of September, at the normal time. Second: In the interests of clarity, the 24th of September is a UN holiday, and the Chamber has considered but finally decided that it will not compensate for the loss of that day by sitting on Friday, the 25th of September. So we'll not sit on that Friday. Finally: It's placed on the record that the week beginning the 12th of October will be a non-sitting week. This doesn't raise any questions, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, what is defined -- what or who are defined as economic migrations?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, economic migrations are all those migrations that take place for economic reasons in search for a better life, a job, et cetera, people go to work somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the 1991 census in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that term utilized?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 1991 census, information was collected about people who left Yugoslavia in order to work abroad. It went without saying that these migrations were economic because simply from 1971, when this information was first collected, there were these organised offices for finding jobs for people abroad, most often in Europe. So there were organised departures to Germany, France, Sweden, et cetera, people were being sent to work there because these countries were looking for a particular structure of people. In the census of 1971, it was the first time that this information was collected and it went that way with all the following censuses. In 1991, the last census in the territory of Yugoslavia was completed, and this category was referred to as citizens temporarily working abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could take a look at 1D5335, that is, again, the original Milosevic report upon which this report for the Mladic case that is in evidence is based, and if we can turn to page 6 in both the English and the Serbian, and it will be the first full paragraph in the English and it will be the second full paragraph in the Serbian. Dr. Tabeau says as follows: "The inclusion of the population abroad could also have impact on the numbers of out-of-country voters (OCV) whom we report as refugees in 1997 to 1998 (see Annex B4). Some 87 per cent of OCV from Bosnia-Herzegovina left the country after the census (the so-called post-census emigration) and did not return home until 1997 to 1998. The remaining 13 per cent resided abroad in 1991 (the pre-census emigration) and remained there after the census in March 1991. If there was no war in Bosnia-Herzegovina the pre-census emigres would perhaps have returned but they registered to vote in 1997/1998 still as out-of-country. We therefore believe that all out-of-country voters may and should be considered as refugees." Professor, what do you have to say here as to the instructions of Ms. Tabeau that all out-of-country voters, including those who had resided out of the country before the census, should be considered refugees for purposes of the demographic work that is being shown in these reports?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no one ever referred to people who left Yugoslavia before 1991 to work abroad as refugees. They were never treated as such. These were citizens of Yugoslavia, who, for economic reasons, went abroad to work. If Dr. Tabeau came to the conclusion that these citizens may and should be considered as refugees, people who left, ten or 20 or 30 years ago, that she should be treated as refugees with the explanation that they could have returned, then, really, she'd have to provide some kind of solution to say whether she interviewed these people somehow, whether there is anything written down to that effect, are there any decisions that people would have want to return precisely then but they could not have because there was a war going on. There's another thing that's of interest here and that is that Dr. Tabeau says that 87 per cent of the voters are outside the country, people who left during the war, that is, again, I have to take her word for it. She does not provide a footnote anywhere saying, In voter registers there were 100.000 people, 5 people, 7 people, who registered as persons who wished to vote from abroad. And it is interesting to note that the pre-census economic migration would not return. That is Ms. Tabeau's position and I don't know on the basis of what, on the basis of which information, on the basis of what kind of figures she presented that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me in saying where Dr. Tabeau says that they left during the war? I see that she says they left the country after the census. Which, in my view, as not the same as during the war. It could be in 1991 to 1992, certain areas. There was no war yet, and if we considered the war to have ended approximately in December 1995, then there's still two years. So where does she say so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. But she says 87 per cent and I don't know where she got the source for the figure, the 87 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that's a different matter and it's not what I asked you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question on that very 87 per cent. You're saying -- the way you explain Dr. Tabeau's report, you say, at line 18 of page 25, "There's another thing that's of interest here and that is that Dr. Tabeau says that 87 per cent of the voters are outside the country." I don't read that to be what Dr. Tabeau says. Dr. Tabeau talks of 87 per cent of the people who are already out of the country, not 87 per cent of the voters. Point number one. Point number two: You just defined a few minutes ago for Mr. Ivetic that people -- economic refugees are people who have left for economic reasons but you say -- you criticise Dr. Tabeau for considering these people where the last sentence as: "We therefore believe that all of out-of-country voters may and should be considered as refugees." She's not characterising these people as refugees from the war. They may very well be economic refugees as you have just defined. Is that possibly -- is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we're understanding each other correctly, Dr. Tabeau says that had there not been a war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the pre-census emigres, well, the census was in 1991, so everybody who left before 1991 perhaps would have returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That does not make the person a war refugee because that's not the reason he left. He left before the war for economic reasons. But refugee still in terms of your definition of economic refugees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But they're not necessarily war refugees. Do you agree on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pre-census emigres, they are not war refugees, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's just what I was saying. So we agree on that. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since we are dealing with definitions I would like to talk you back to the beginning of today's hearing, on page 2, lines 20 and 21. You said: "... concerning refugees and internally displaced persons, we usually use the UN definition." Can you explain the UN definition of "refugees and internally displaced persons"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can paraphrase because I cannot quote it verbatim but I could bring it, if you wish. Refugees are all peoples whose lives are threatened in different ways and who had to leave their country. That is to say, they had to leave the country. Whereas displaced persons are all persons who within the same territory, again, for a variety of reasons, had to move within the same territory. Internally displaced persons do not have to be displaced only because of a war. For example, maybe a dam was being built on a river and an entire settlement had to be sunk and then these people had to be internally displaced. They had to be relocated to a different area of the same country. All the displaced persons from Kosovo-Metohija are treated in Serbia as internally displaced persons, not refugees, simply because it is a single state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And what is the difference between this definition and that of Ms. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Tabeau does not provide a single definition. She says we use statistical definitions and she doesn't explain any of that. And then she considers under this statistical definition that all refugees -- or, rather, that all economic migrants can be counted as refugees because perhaps they'd return. That's what Ms. Tabeau says. They may and should be considered as refugees. Now what Ms. Tabeau considers to be an internally displaced person, that's a different story. If you're willing to hear me out, I can explain that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we have that in the report. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Professor, you have a couple of times used the term "broader context" in talking about these reports. Can you tell us what you -- what you consider when you use that term?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the term "broader context" is used by Prosecution experts. They don't explain it. I think I spoke about that yesterday, a bit. They don't say what it is. They use sources of information or data that have nothing to do with the years to which the indictment pertains. For example, they used the census of 1991 and the voters' registers of 1997. That is broader context for them. It's not only two sources of data that can be used as broader context and two years only. If they're using this, they have to explain why and it cannot pertain only to data sources that do not coincide with those years that are indispensable for her to make analysis. She says for such and such a period, regardless of the report and the indictee involved we have no information and that is why we're going to use 1991 and 1997 as far as ethnic changes are concerned. And then that is broader context. I cannot say, because Dr. Tabeau uses terms "ethnic cleansing" and some others, this or that, whether that falls within this broader context. But she does not define it anywhere. Then it would be clearer had see defined it. On the basis of what she writes, it only refers to sources of data considerably earlier, considerably later, certain years considerably earlier or later, what she could get. And it's not the years for which the report was being written.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could take a look together at 1D5340. This will again be the publication by Dr. Tabeau: Conflict in Numbers. And we'll need page 16 in English, page 13 in Serbian. That will be on the bottom of page of in English and the second-to-last paragraph in the Serbian. And in English, it's starting with the second line in the last paragraph, the sentence that starts: "Secondly," and it goes: "Secondly and perhaps more importantly, probative standards at ICTY in relation to genocide" --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I haven't got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. If we can have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly where in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph, we see on the bottom it's the second line and starts: "Secondly." It should be page 13 in the Serbian and it will be the second-to-last paragraph in the Serbian version. I see we have again the English version. So we need the Serbian version. That's the problem. And if we could zoom in it will be the second-to-last paragraph in the Serbian version and in the second line of that paragraph and it at the very end of that second line where it starts [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Secondly, and perhaps more importantly, probative standards at ICTY in relation to genocide and other crimes against humanity have been high. These crimes are not random events; there was a collective policy of extermination behind them. The systematic and planned nature of the crimes requires that proving them must be based on presenting documentation and analysis that go far beyond the crime itself. Showing the broader context and longer duration than in conventional cases is 'a must' at the Tribunals, such as ICTY." Professor, as a demographer, do you have any comment as to Dr. Tabeau's words here that we've just read?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this first part, if Ms. Tabeau already knows that this is systematic destruction, et cetera, she had to put a footnote there and say, How come? Where did she see that? On the basis of which documents did she conclude that, right? As for the second part, invoking a broader context, she says that that became a must, in The Hague Tribunal. Again, I'm saying that there is an explanation missing, a footnotes missing, who is it that made this a must? Is it the Office of the Prosecutor? Is it the International Tribunal as such in general terms or do experts believe that this is a must? And if it is a must, they should say why it is a must. Why a broader context is a must.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, depending on who gave the objective that it must show a broader context, would that affect the reports that would be generated?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if something is an imperative, then it certainly has to affect things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 1D5334, and this will be the report of Dr. Tabeau for the Bosanski Samac and Odzak case that you had mentioned earlier on. And it will be page 1 in the Serbian and page 11 in the English. And, again, we seem to have the Serbian and the English flipped on the monitor. And the first part says: "This report summarizes changes in the ethnic composition of two municipalities in the northeastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bosanski Samac and Odzak, between 1991 and 1997. Our goal is to provide reliable demographic statistics and allow for an assessment of the type and scale of the changes. In our study, we analyse two data sources: The 1991 population census and 1997 voters' register, and use standard statistical and demographic methods." Now, I'll stop right there and I'll ask you: In terms of the reference using standard statistical and demographic methods, do you agree what is represented here as to that report, first of all, and then the reports that were used in this case, for the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The standard statistical method for matching is not used by them. They use a modified method for matching, and we saw that yesterday. If you are not using standard statistical methods, then you cannot obtain standard statistical measures, and even less so if you have sources containing so many errors can you achieve a result that makes it possible to arrive at reliable statistical data. What kind of reliability can we talk about if the voters' register does not contain information about ethnicity in 100 per cent of cases? Prosecution experts get it by searching for it during matching. If somebody matches, then this is a Serb, a Croat, or a Muslim. And we already have seen how the matching was done. So you are taking over a datum from somewhere and it would be okay if it's taken over by -- in a standard way. You can say I have 100 voters and I have managed to match 50 but that is not said anywhere. This is neither a standard measure nor a standard statistical result.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, Professor, do those criticisms relate only to the Samac report, or do they also relate to the reports that were entered into evidence for the Mladic case?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports submitted in the Mladic case and all the reports that I've had occasion to read and were done in this way. I referred only to certain reports in the bibliography for the Mladic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to page 29 in Serbian on -- that we have on the screen and page 33 in English and it will be the first paragraph under 3.3: Final conclusions [sic]. "Summing up, two clear examples of ethnic cleansing have been shown in this report: Croats and Muslims largely disappeared from the Serb Samac and from the Serb Odzak (Vukosavlje). Before the war in both these areas Croats and Muslims represented a considerable fraction of the actual population." Professor, is it appropriate for a demographer to set forth such a conclusion in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this case, the Court can make a decision whether ethnic cleansing was involved or not. A demographer has to show the change in ethnic structure and he can make a conclusion that it's changed significantly or less significantly. He should certainly not say that it is a clear example of ethnic cleansing. An expert makes judgements on the situations that he reviews and then he presents the results and leaves it to the trier of fact to decide whether it is ethnic cleansing or not. There is no documentation here to justify such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, can you help me to understand what you are saying. You said, you talked about ethnic cleansing. Where do we find the word "ethnic cleansing" in the text that was read to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First line, middle of the sentence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, I'll ask you to repeat the last part of your answer because I'm not sure that the translation came in -- let me ask the question; maybe it will be quicker. Is ethnic cleansing a word what is defined and normally used in the field of demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That concept is not defined in demography. When demographers do something, they take over the definition of ethnic cleansing from the United Nations. There is no demographic definition of ethnic cleansing which doesn't mean, of course, that demographers writing certain papers do not mention ethnic cleansing. But when they do, they always define what they understand by ethnic cleansing. Demography as a science does not have a definition for ethnic cleansing. If authors and scientists deal with that, then they take over definitions from the United Nations or from wherever they please, but then they include it in a footnote, saying, By ethnic cleansing, we mean this, this, and that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to look at 1D5340 again. And this time it will be page 25, bleeding onto page 26 in the Serbian and page 24, bleeding over to page 25 in the English, starting at the bottom of the page and this is, again: Conflict in Numbers by Dr. Tabeau. And it relates to something that you testified about earlier when talking generally. And if ... it is the sixth line from the bottom in the English --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Could you make this a bit larger. I can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it will be in the middle of the ... I think the seventh line from the bottom in the Serbian where Dr. Tabeau says: "Noteworthy, all reports on the BH ethnic composition, and IDPs and refugees were made in the framework of one and the same project run at the OTP between 1998 and 2003. The project was meant for use in the Slobodan Milosevic trial but we made all calculations for all municipalities in the country; we even wrote a computer programme" --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if we can go to the next page in the Serbian. And if we could zoom in.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm continuing: "We even wrote a computer programme that automatically generated the text explaining statistics. So, I was possible to re-run our calculations and to make identical reports for any area in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In this" --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we need to turn the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "In this way, several reports were presented in a number of cases. The Defence occasionally complained about us repeating our approach. However, we made it our principle to keep things unchanged in all projects on IDPs, refugees, and ethnic composition, as we believe the incredible effort we made to complete this work was worth it." Do you have a comment as to what Dr. Tabeau has said here?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they completed everything in the period between 1997, 1998 and 2003 and computerised everything and if, for certain sections, I just need to press a button for the programme to release information about certain municipalities, then they completed it all by 2003. Since there were critiques and objections, they still decided not to change anything because a huge amount of work and effort had been invested. A huge amount of work an effort is not a good criterion if something needs to be corrected or improved. If they all finished everything by 2003, and since then I've heard of new methods that are better or found information that my method was bad, incorrect, then I would obviously need to change it, if they finished everything in 2003, then I don't understand why they stayed on, why they didn't just go home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But in this statement here, it is being said that the complaint was not because the methods used were wrong but the complaint was that they were repeating themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If I'm repeating myself but I'm correct, do I have to change my ways?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, you are not right. When she says here that they are repeating themselves, they are referring to that model. We have created one model and we applied it to everything. She doesn't refer to, for instance, objections made by other experts and with every report you take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I hear what you say. You're criticising the fact that she is not changing her model because she invested a lot of time there it. And I'm saying that the criticism that I see on this document of for not changing the model is because she repeats herself. Not because she is wrong as you suggested that if you use a wrong model and you must change it. That's the only question I'm asking. You are introducing a different reason for the objection. You are saying because what you did was wrong. But in the paper -- in this document, they say because she is repeating herself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was written by Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That word is hers. Would she believe that she would criticise herself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then are you rewriting the report for her. You're saying that the reason they are objecting was because she did something wrong. You are not sticking to what she is saying that they were repeating themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not changing the content. The counsel was asking me for a comment on this passage in the text. I am saying that it's absurd for someone who has had occasion to hear that he is making errors, that his method is wrong, that his sources are not good to continue doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Precisely why I'm asking you this question. She is not saying here that she was told her methods were wrong. She's saying she is was told that she is repeating herself. Now are you introducing that her methods were wrong. She's saying this criticism that I'm repeating myself, I -- I didn't change because I put a lot of effort into it the -- I'm not being criticised on the basis that what I'm saying is wrong. I'm being criticised on the basis that I'm repeating myself. Now, the question of wrong things is being introduced by you, not by this statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I'm understanding you right. If Dr. Tabeau is writing this article, she will choose the word that suits her, not the critique addressed to her earlier. Would you really believe that she would ever write the Defence has criticised me because I applied a bad method, that my sources were bad, et cetera? The Defence never objected because she was repeating herself but because the method applied was the one created in 2003 where you press a button and you get information on a municipality. Every report is done in the same way, it only refers to different cases. In every report the same sources are used, the same non-demographic measures are used. Statistical definitions that don't exist are used, and all that repeats itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are saying, in fact, that she is hiding the fact she's being criticised for being wrong and therefore not going to call herself wrong she uses the word "repeat." So you are rewriting this document for her. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could try to clarify a bit further because there may be some difference of understanding. You are reading the report as saying whatever criticism there will be, I'll never change my mind. What she says is, I want to be consistent in my presentation. We have developed tools for that, and the fact that it may look repetitious is for me not a reason to change anything. Whereas you are criticizing her for something which she apparently, but correct me if I'm wrong, did not say. That is, whatever criticism comes, even if correct, even if it's criticism about standards, et cetera, et cetera, I'll never change my mind. That's what you're commenting on, and that's -- from what we see is not what she says.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, now you've changed Ms. Tabeau's words and now you're not using her words either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm paraphrasing but I do that to illustrate what may happen into court. And if you say but -- let me say the following. The examples given come approximately down to whatever the criticism is. Of course, that's not the words used by the witness. That's my interpretation of what the witness said in order to clarify what's apparently is an issue which is in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, let me ask you this way. This book by Dr. Tabeau was published, I believe, in 2009. In the, I believe, five prior cases that you appeared as an expert for, what type of complaints did you make about Dr. Tabeau's work. Were they based upon repetition or something else?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something else. With every report, I concentrated on methodology, and in every report, as I've been saying now, I'm saying that the methodology they apply is not scientific methodology. The reports they present to the Court are not based on scientific professional methodology, nor can they provide adequate data. With every report, I dealt only with methodology and showed that this methodology does not hold up. It's not scientific. It's unique. And it's applied only here at this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Mr. Ivetic, this sentence on top of the document, doesn't deal with witnesses but with the Defence and their complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 23 in English, and it's the last part of the second-to-last paragraph; and in Serbian, it's page 24, and it's the end of the first paragraph on the page. And it will start the last line of that second-to-last paragraph in English and it will be the last line of the paragraph referenced in -- in Serbian. And it says: "Like it or not, it has been a remarkable achievement of this small group to make this kind of contribution to the field of demography of war in general and to the ICTY expert testimonies on demographics, in particular." Now, fist, I'd like to ask you: What is this demography of war that she is talking about?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Demography is a science which has its various disciplines, like many other sciences. War demography is as a discipline of demography is not something I've ever heard of. I first heard Dr. Brunborg refer to it by saying that he will make an initiative for the introduction of war demography. Whether it was really introduced and whether that is accepted or not, I don't know. But I've never heard of a concept called "war demography," just as I believe that there is no war demographers, another term that I've heard. You are either a demographer or not a demographer, and you deal with various areas. Nobody specialised to such an accident that they call themselves a birth-rate demographer or a historical demographer. I myself taught ethno-demography. You may choose one or another area and dedicate yourself to it but I've never heard of terms "war demography" and "war demographer," and I don't know at least that it's accepted as something that exists in the world. And when I say exists, I mean I haven't heard of the existence of a scientific discipline called war demography as a part of the science of demography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I -- oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where do I find that there is something like a discipline of war demography? Where does Ms. Tabeau say that? And that it is a scientific discipline.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nowhere. And I'm saying it doesn't exist. I've never heard it. Maybe Dr. Tabeau heard of it. But this demography that she's dealing with here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you -- you explained at length that discipline of war demography doesn't exist. Why didn't you explain that with reference to this sentence. I didn't find anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is there. Field of demography of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... Your Honour, here it is. "Great contribution" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Don't interrupt me. I know the difference between a field and scientific discipline and what was the other term? Discipline of war demography. I'm not talking about field. I'm talking about the words used by the witness. And I would like to know where we can find that in the text read out by Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't find the word the "discipline." You can find the word "field of war demography." Last line here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clarifies the matter, what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn to page 25 in English and page 28 in Serbian, it will be the second-to-last paragraph in English; and it will be the middle of the second-to-last paragraph in the Serbian. And it's the middle of the paragraph in both languages and it's the phrase that starts: "Whenever a demographic expert report is admitted, the likely consequence is" --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It will be on page 28, the second-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Whenever a demographic expert report is admitted, the likely consequence is that the report has impact on the judgement." What would you like to bring to our attention in relation to Dr. Tabeau's observation here?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If she wrote something like that, she was probably aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to a different topic. Dr. Brunborg when he testified here at transcript page 15168 to 15169, talked about a topic, and I'd like to read for you so you get the translation of the testimony. Then I'll have some questions about it: "Q. Okay. Now as part of your mandate and your task that you received from the Office of the Prosecutor, were you asked to pay attention to the status of persons so as to differentiate between those registered as soldiers and those that were not? "A. No, I was not. "Q. Was any part of your tasking or mandate concerned with differentiating whether persons had gone missing as part of the column of Bosnian Muslim males that left Srebrenica and went through the woods to try and break through to Tuzla? "A. No, I was not. But I would like to add, as to the first part of the question, attention to the status of persons being soldiers that we, after I left, my colleagues acquired lists on, from the Bosnian army who had gone, been killed, and -- and this list was merged with the list of missing, and 70 per cent of those who are reported as missing were also listed by the army as having been killed, but the army did not list any place of disappearance or cause of, or cause of death or place of death, whether it was in combat or not, they listed death, date of death, but that appeared to be -- the quality of that information appeared to be poor." Okay. Now I think the translation has ended. Now, so from that testimony of Dr. Brunborg focussed on the fact that the lists from the army did not list cause or place of death, did the sources that Dr. Tabeau and Dr. Brunborg relied upon, the other sources, did those sources always provide place and cause of death.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No source, save for the last one, being the International Commission for Missing Persons, they were the only ones to cite the place of death. No other source, as far as I know, did not list the cause of death. How far, I have to point out yet again that I don't know everything that's in the database of the Demographic Unit because I only know -- or, actually, I only saw certain sources of information. However, when it comes to the sources used in the drafting of reports, with the exception of the international centre for identifying missing person, no other source listed the cause or place of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Professor, did you ever have occasion to perform your own analysis on the Prosecution list of victims from Srebrenica to ascertain if it included soldiers who did not die in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 2007 or 2008, I visited the Demographic Unit, and I did that for the first time using the ABiH list and the list of victims used by the OTP. I carried out a matching process, according to all of the applicable rules. First, I realised that there were soldiers on the list. Up until that point, in no report about Srebrenica was there any mention that there were soldiers. On the contrary, Dr. Brunborg, in his 2003 report, claims that they are non-fighters. So that was the first time that it was discovered that there are soldiers on their lists. And in 2009 in this report, they say that they were 70 per cent. I forgot the second part of the question. I apologise. Yes, yes. In comparing the information contained on the army list and the list drafted by the OTP experts, there were soldiers considered as killed by the ABiH before July 1995, having been killed in 1992, 1993, 1994, or early in 1995; before July. Of course, I provided that information to the counsel, and they must have forwarded it. That is minimum proof, if I may say so, because it relies on a single source of information which testifies to the fact that on the OTP expert list, there are people who did not die in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we're at the time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is time for a break. Yes, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it is a while ago that the Registrar informed me that the net time had you used was three hours and 31 minutes. And that's already a while ago. Can you give us any indication as to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have exactly 15 questions left.

utterances.text: Overall, I had 135.
